core_obligations: Choose a covering of the target and, over each member, coverings of the two base changed sources, and observe that the fibre products of corresponding members are affine formal algebraic spaces and countably indexed (proof lines 5235-5245).
Note that those fibre products form a covering of the fibre product of the two sources, so that the equivalent conditions may be verified on them (proof lines 5246-5248).
Observe that the projection from each piece to the third space factors through the corresponding member of its covering (proof lines 5248-5250).

Identify the piece with the formal spectrum of the completed tensor product of the two rings, and conclude by stability of the property under base change, using the property of the original ring map supplied by the hypothesis (proof lines 5250-5263).
proof_roadmap: The pieces cover the fibre product (proof lines 5246-5248).
Identification of the pieces as completed tensor products (proof lines 5250-5257).
Transfer of the property by base change stability (proof lines 5257-5263).
difficulty_reason: Given a local property P of morphisms of complete weakly admissible rings which is stable under base change, and morphisms of locally countably indexed formal algebraic spaces from X and Z to Y, the lemma asserts that if the morphism from X to Y satisfies the equivalent conditions of the preceding lemma then so does the projection from the fibre product to Z (statement lines 5225-5233). The proof reduces to the affine case by coverings: a covering of the target is chosen and, over each member, coverings of the two base changes; the fibre products of corresponding members are affine formal algebraic spaces and countably indexed by an earlier lemma, and they form a covering of the fibre product of the two sources (proof lines 5235-5248). Since the projections from these pieces to the third space factor through the chosen covers of that space, it suffices to see that the ring map obtained by completing the tensor product has the property, which the assumption on the original ring map together with stability under base change gives directly (proof lines 5248-5263). The claim is H2: the covering reduction, the identification of the affine pieces as formal spectra of completed tensor products, and the transfer of the property are each carried out, with the only external input being the identification of the fibre product of two affine pieces.
